boards.title: Your First Weekend at Trinity University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe campus sequence: orient yourself, eat, explore landmark spaces, and leave time to recharge.

cards.title: Start by getting your bearings
cards.subtitle: Trinity University campus
cards.notes: Use Trinity’s self-guided tour as an opening loop, then save the places that catch your attention for a slower return later in the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A flexible first look at campus before you settle into the rest of the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity’s visit page links visitors to a self-guided campus tour.
cards.access_notes: Use Trinity’s visit page to access the self-guided tour and confirm current visitor information.

cards.title: Pause at Miller Fountain
cards.subtitle: Campus landmark
cards.notes: Build in a short outdoor pause at the fountain during your campus loop; it is an easy named landmark to use as a regrouping point.
cards.short_summary: A historic fountain that anchors a brief outdoor campus stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies the Eugenia B. Miller Fountain as a campus destination and says it was presented to the university in 1966.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access and any nearby event setup can vary; follow campus signage.

cards.title: Make a meal plan at Mabee
cards.subtitle: First-year area, lower campus
cards.notes: Choose a meal window and look over the available stations together; Mabee lists breakfast, lunch, dinner, and several meal formats.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus all-you-care-to-eat dining hall in the first-year area.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says Mabee Dining Hall offers breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with international, made-to-order, grill, deli, and vegan/vegetarian choices.
cards.access_notes: Dining access and service times can change; check current campus dining information before going.

cards.title: Claim a study-table reset
cards.subtitle: 1 Trinity Place
cards.notes: Take a quiet break to browse, sketch out the week ahead, or reserve a study room if you need a shared place to work.
cards.short_summary: A library stop with study-room reservations, research help, and special collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Coates Library offers study-room reservations, librarian support, research guides, and special collections and archives.
cards.access_notes: Building and service hours vary, including during breaks; consult the library’s current hours page.

cards.title: Find the Magic Stones
cards.subtitle: Near Coates Library and the Center for the Sciences and Innovation
cards.notes: Walk over to the sculpture and use its surrounding outdoor area for a conversation or photo, then continue your campus circuit.
cards.short_summary: A named Barbara Hepworth sculpture and longstanding Trinity gathering landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity identifies “A Conversation with Magic Stones” as a Barbara Hepworth sculpture near Coates Library and the Center for the Sciences and Innovation.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor artwork; respect the sculpture and any posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Look up at Murchison Tower
cards.subtitle: Campus skyline landmark
cards.notes: Use the tower as a visual waypoint while you cross campus; keep the visit ground-level unless a university program specifically opens other access.
cards.short_summary: A 1964 campus tower that holds the Carolyn Calvert Bells.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says the T. Frank Murchison Memorial Tower, which holds the Carolyn Calvert Bells, became a campus landmark in 1964.
cards.access_notes: Do not assume tower access; participate only in university-authorized programs and follow posted restrictions.

cards.title: Take a reflective chapel stop
cards.subtitle: Western edge of campus, by Murchison Bell Tower
cards.notes: Visit the chapel area for a quiet reset and notice the adjacent meditation garden; keep the stop respectful of worship and scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: A chapel and meditation-garden setting beside the Murchison Bell Tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says Parker Chapel is on the western edge of campus by the Murchison Bell Tower and includes a meditation garden with three fountains.
cards.source_title: Margarite B. Parker Chapel | Trinity University
cards.access_notes: The building has special hours that may change; respect services, events, and campus access guidance.

cards.title: Locate the Bell Athletic Center
cards.subtitle: Trinity athletic complex
cards.notes: Walk past the athletic complex to understand where recreation and varsity events happen, then check official schedules before planning another visit.
cards.short_summary: The hub of Trinity’s athletic complex, with gyms, a natatorium, and sports-performance space.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity describes the Bell Athletic Center as the center of its athletic complex, housing two gymnasiums, a natatorium, and a sports performance center.
cards.access_notes: Facility entry and event attendance depend on current schedules and access rules.

cards.title: Grab an on-the-go bite at Coates Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus dining area
cards.notes: Use this as a flexible midday food stop between campus landmarks; choose from the named dining counters listed by Trinity for the current day.
cards.short_summary: A campus commons with multiple quick-service dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says Coates Commons is home to Einstein Bros. Bagels, Taste of San Antonio, Legends Burger Co., and Crave.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current operators, menus, and service times with campus dining before visiting.

cards.title: End with a Skyline view
cards.subtitle: Second level of the Coates Student Center
cards.notes: Save this for a relaxed lunch or an early meal after your campus loop; the dining room is documented as having views toward downtown.
cards.short_summary: A Coates Student Center dining room with downtown views.
cards.evidence_claim: Trinity says the Skyline Dining Room is on the second level of the Coates Student Center and offers views of downtown.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current dining service and access details with campus dining before visiting.
